requirements: Interact with the maze environment one action at a time using the move tool.
Navigate from S to E in each maze episode.
Use only Up, Down, Left, or Right moves; diagonal movement is not allowed.
Locate and collect K before attempting to pass through D.
Avoid traps when possible or account for the 5-move penalty when entering T.
Use feedback after every action to update knowledge of the maze.

Maintain persistent knowledge of visited cells, blocked cells, successful moves, failed moves, dead ends, trap locations, key locations, door locations, successful strategies, failed strategies, mistakes, and their causes.
Avoid repeating actions or strategies that have already been learned to be unsuccessful.
Record environmental patterns, hazards, useful exploration techniques, and mistakes with their causes.
Complete each episode within the limited number of moves.
success_criteria: The agent reaches E from S within the allowed move limit.
If a locked door D is on the solution path, the agent has collected K before passing through D.
All moves are legal cardinal moves and do not pass through # or through D before K is collected.
The agent uses feedback to correctly update its knowledge of the maze.
The agent avoids previously identified unsuccessful actions and does not repeatedly make the same mistakes.
The agent records and can use successful and failed strategies, hazards, dead ends, trap/key/door locations, and mistake causes.
The agent demonstrates persistent learning across maze episodes.
known_info: Cell symbols include S for start, E for exit, . for open cell, # for wall, K for key, D for locked door, and T for trap.
The agent starts at S and must reach E.
The agent can move only Up, Down, Left, or Right.
Right increases x, Left decreases x, Up increases y, and Down decreases y.
The locked door D cannot be passed until the key K has been collected.
Entering a trap T is allowed but adds a 5-move penalty.
The agent receives feedback after every action.
Each episode has a limited number of moves.
The agent initially knows the rules but not the maze layout.
The solution path is never provided.
The available environment tool is move, which moves one cell in a cardinal direction.
The benchmark is described as persistent maze learning, so the agent is expected to retain and use knowledge beyond a single action or potentially across episodes.
unknown_info: The actual layout of each maze episode.
The positions of S, E, K, D, T, walls, and open cells in each episode.
The exact move limit for each episode and whether it varies by maze size.
The exact format and information content of the feedback after each action.
Whether every maze contains a key, door, and traps, and whether there can be multiple keys, doors, or traps.
The exact number of episodes and whether each episode uses a new layout or repeats one.
Whether the key is consumed on use or remains after opening the door.
Whether the trap penalty is applied immediately, whether it can cause an episode to end early, and whether trap locations are revealed by feedback.
The precise coordinate system origin and grid indexing.
constraints: Only cardinal movement is allowed; diagonals are forbidden.
Movement through D is impossible until K is collected.
Traps T do not block movement but incur a 5-move penalty.
Each episode has a limited move budget.
Only one action can be taken per interaction.
The solution path is never provided.
The agent must maintain specified knowledge categories.
The agent should avoid repeating known unsuccessful actions.
The agent must rely on its own strategy, feedback, and memory.
available_actions: Use move with direction Up, Down, Left, or Right.
Observe feedback returned after each move.
Update internal memory with visited cells, blocked cells, successful moves, failed moves, dead ends, traps, keys, and doors.
Record successful and failed strategies, environmental patterns, hazards, exploration techniques, and mistakes with causes.
Plan the next move, backtrack from dead ends, and avoid known bad moves.
Choose and adapt an exploration or navigation strategy.
expected_challenges: The maze layout is initially unknown, so the agent must explore efficiently under a limited move budget.
The key must be found before the locked door can be crossed, potentially requiring backtracking.
Traps impose a 5-move penalty that can exhaust the move budget.
The agent must remember and use a large amount of state information across actions and possibly episodes.
Avoiding repeated unsuccessful actions while still exploring unknown areas can be difficult.
Feedback may be partial or ambiguous, making it hard to infer the full maze structure.
Dead ends, loops, and misleading corridors can waste moves.
Balancing exploration for key discovery with exploitation toward the exit is nontrivial.
Persistent learning across episodes may require generalizing from previous layouts without assuming they are identical.
